Five tetrahedra inscribed in a dodecahedron. Five opposing tetrahedra (not shown) can also be inscribed.

As two opposing tetrahedra can be inscribed in a cube, and five cubes can be inscribed in a dodecahedron, ten tetrahedra in five cubes can be inscribed in a dodecahedron: two opposing sets of five, with each set covering all 20 vertices and each vertex in two tetrahedra (one from each set, but not the opposing pair). As stated by [Coxeter et al. (1938)](#CITEREFCoxeterdu_ValFlatherPetrie1938),[[15]](#cite_note-coxeter-1938-15)

> "Just as a tetrahedron can be inscribed in a cube, so a cube can be inscribed in a dodecahedron. By reciprocation, this leads to an octahedron circumscribed about an icosahedron. In fact, each of the twelve vertices of the icosahedron divides an edge of the octahedron according to the "[golden section](/wiki/Golden_section "Golden section")". Given the icosahedron, the circumscribed octahedron can be chosen in five ways, giving a [compound of five octahedra](/wiki/Compound_of_five_octahedra "Compound of five octahedra"), which comes under our definition of [stellated icosahedron](/wiki/Stellated_icosahedron "Stellated icosahedron"). (The reciprocal compound, of five cubes whose vertices belong to a dodecahedron, is a stellated [triacontahedron](/wiki/Triacontahedron "Triacontahedron").) Another stellated icosahedron can at once be deduced, by stellating each octahedron into a [stella octangula](/wiki/Stella_octangula "Stella octangula"), thus forming a [compound of ten tetrahedra](/wiki/Compound_of_ten_tetrahedra "Compound of ten tetrahedra"). Major Allied offensives in the Pacific began in August 1942 with the [Guadalcanal](/wiki/Guadalcanal_campaign "Guadalcanal campaign") and [New Guinea campaigns](/wiki/New_Guinea_campaign "New Guinea campaign"). These were followed by [Operation Cartwheel](/wiki/Operation_Cartwheel "Operation Cartwheel") from June 1943, which neutralized the major Japanese base at [Rabaul](/wiki/Rabaul "Rabaul") on New Britain by early 1944. Elsewhere, Allied forces recaptured the Aleutian Islands by August 1943, and initiated the [Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign](/wiki/Gilbert_and_Marshall_Islands_campaign "Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign") in November 1943, which lasted until February 1944. In the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea "Battle of the Philippine Sea") in June 1944, the Japanese fleet took heavy damage; the Allied [campaign to recapture the Philippines](/wiki/Philippines_campaign_(1944%E2%80%931945) "Philippines campaign (1944–1945)") began in October and set off the [Battle of Leyte Gulf](/wiki/Battle_of_Leyte_Gulf "Battle of Leyte Gulf"), after which the Japanese were unable to fight further surface engagements and resorted to *[kamikaze](/wiki/Kamikaze "Kamikaze")* attacks. The rest of the war was characterized by an Allied strategy of [island hopping](/wiki/Leapfrogging_(strategy) "Leapfrogging (strategy)"), with [invasions of the Mariana and Palau Islands](/wiki/Mariana_and_Palau_Islands_campaign "Mariana and Palau Islands campaign"), [Iwo Jima](/wiki/Battle_of_Iwo_Jima "Battle of Iwo Jima"), and [Okinawa](/wiki/Battle_of_Okinawa "Battle of Okinawa") between June 1944 and June 1945. William McKinley Jr. was born in 1843 in [Niles, Ohio](/wiki/Niles,_Ohio "Niles, Ohio"), the seventh of nine children of [William McKinley Sr.](/wiki/William_McKinley_Sr. "William McKinley Sr.") and Nancy (née Allison) McKinley.[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeech4Morgan2-2) The McKinleys were of [English](/wiki/English_Americans "English Americans") and [Scots-Irish](/wiki/Scotch-Irish_Americans "Scotch-Irish Americans") descent and had settled in western Pennsylvania in the 18th century. Their immigrant ancestor was David McKinley, born in [Dervock](/wiki/Dervock "Dervock"), County Antrim, in present-day [Northern Ireland](/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"). William McKinley Sr. was born in Pennsylvania, in [Pine Township, Mercer County](/wiki/Pine_Township,_Mercer_County,_Pennsylvania "Pine Township, Mercer County, Pennsylvania").[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeech4Morgan2-2)

The family moved to Ohio when the senior McKinley was a boy, settling in [New Lisbon](/wiki/Lisbon,_Ohio "Lisbon, Ohio") (now Lisbon). He met Nancy Allison there, and they married later.[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeech4Morgan2-2) The Allison family was of mostly English descent and among Pennsylvania's earliest settlers.[[2]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorgan3-3) The family trade on both sides was iron making. Ward Jr.](/wiki/Steve_Ward_(businessman) "Steve Ward (businessman)") Ward was succeeded by [William Amelio](/wiki/William_Amelio "William Amelio") on 20 December 2005. In February 2009, Yang replaced Amelio as CEO and has served in that capacity ever since. Yang was chairman of Lenovo's board from 2004 to 2008, and returned as chairman in 2012 alongside his role as CEO.

In 2012, Yang received a $3 million bonus as a reward for record profits, which he in turn redistributed to about 10,000 of Lenovo's employees. According to Lenovo spokesman, Jeffrey Shafer, Yang felt that it would be the right thing to, "redirect [the money] to the employees as a real tangible gesture for what they done." Shafer also said that Yang, who owns about eight per cent of Lenovo's stock, "felt that he was rewarded well simply as the owner of the company".[[196]](#cite_note-Bonus-196) The bonuses were mostly distributed among staff working in positions such as production and reception who received an average of CN¥2,000 or about US$314. **Ventura**, officially the **City of San Buenaventura** (Spanish for "[Saint Bonaventure](/wiki/Saint_Bonaventure "Saint Bonaventure")"),[[11]](#cite_note-11) is a city in and the [county seat](/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Ventura County, California](/wiki/Ventura_County,_California "Ventura County, California"), United States. It is a coastal city located northwest of [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"). The population was 110,763 at the [2020 United States census](/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census").[[12]](#cite_note-12) Ventura is a popular tourist destination, owing to its historic landmarks, beaches, and resorts.

Ventura has been inhabited by different peoples, including the Chumash Native Americans, for at least 10,000 years.[[13]](#cite_note-13) With the arrival of Spanish missionaries in 1782, [Mission San Buenaventura](/wiki/Mission_San_Buenaventura "Mission San Buenaventura") was established by [Junípero Serra](/wiki/Jun%C3%ADpero_Serra "Junípero Serra"), giving the city its name.[[14]](#cite_note-14) Following the [Mexican secularization act of 1833](/wiki/Mexican_secularization_act_of_1833 "Mexican secularization act of 1833"), San Buenaventura was granted by Governor [Pío Pico](/wiki/P%C3%ADo_Pico "Pío Pico") to [Don](/wiki/Don_(honorific) "Don (honorific)") José de Arnaz as [Rancho Ex-Mission San Buenaventura](/wiki/Rancho_Ex-Mission_San_Buenaventura "Rancho Ex-Mission San Buenaventura") and a small community arose. Following the American [Conquest of California](/wiki/Conquest_of_California "Conquest of California"), San Buenaventura was eventually incorporated as a city in 1866. The 1920s brought a major oil boom which significantly developed and expanded Ventura, a growth that continued with the [post–World War II economic expansion](/wiki/Post%E2%80%93World_War_II_economic_expansion "Post–World War II economic expansion").

[Polycystic kidney disease](/wiki/Polycystic_kidney_disease "Polycystic kidney disease") (PKD) which causes kidney failure in affected adult cats has an incidence rate of 36–49% in the Persian breed.[[71]](#cite_note-71) A study in Japan of cats suspected to have kidney problems found that 46% of tested Persian cats had the PKD1 mutation, which is responsible for feline polycystic kidney disease (PKD).[[72]](#cite_note-72) Previous [ultrasonographic](/wiki/Ultrasonograph "Ultrasonograph") studies (involving procedures likely to be performed on cats suspected of kidney problems) found a PKD rate in Persian and related breeds of 49.2% in the UK, 43% in Australia, and 41.8% in France.[[73]](#cite_note-73) The cause of PKD in the Persian is an [autosomal dominant](/wiki/Autosomal_dominant "Autosomal dominant") mutation to the [PKD1](/wiki/PKD1 "PKD1") gene.[[74]](#cite_note-74)

Cysts develop and grow in the kidney over time, replacing kidney tissues and enlarging the kidney. Kidney failure develops later in life, at an average age of 7 years old (ranging from 3 to 10 years old). Symptoms include excessive drinking and urination, reduced appetite, weight loss, and depression.[[75]](#cite_note-75) The disease is [autosomal dominant](/wiki/Autosomal_dominant "Autosomal dominant") and DNA screening is the preferred method of eliminating the gene in the breed. Because of DNA testing, most responsible Persian breeders now have cats that no longer carry the PKD gene, hence their offspring also do not have the gene. Before DNA screening was available, an ultrasound was done. However, an ultrasound is only as good as the day that it is done, and many cats that were thought to be clear, were in fact, a carrier of the PKD gene. Only DNA screening and breeding cats that are negative for the PKD gene will produce kittens that are also negative for the gene, effectively removing this gene from the breeding pool.[[76]](#cite_note-76)

*How the Grinch Stole Christmas* grossed $265.5 million domestically and $85.1 million in other territories, for a worldwide total gross of $350.6 million,[[5]](#cite_note-NUM-6) making it the [sixth-highest-grossing film of 2000](/wiki/2000_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2000 in film").

In the United States, the film earned $15.6 million on its opening day. Over the weekend, it grossed $55.1 million, with an average of $17,615 from 3,127 theaters.[[59]](#cite_note-61) At the time of its release, it held the sixth-highest-grossing three-day opening weekend of any film, trailing behind *[Toy Story 2](/wiki/Toy_Story_2 "Toy Story 2")*, *[X-Men](/wiki/X-Men_(film) "X-Men (film)")*, *[Mission: Impossible 2](/wiki/Mission:_Impossible_2 "Mission: Impossible 2")*, *[Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace](/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_%E2%80%93_The_Phantom_Menace "Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace")* and *[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](/wiki/The_Lost_World:_Jurassic_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")*.[[60]](#cite_note-62) Additionally, it surpassed *[Batman Forever](/wiki/Batman_Forever "Batman Forever")* to secure the largest opening weekend for a [Jim Carrey](/wiki/Jim_Carrey "Jim Carrey") film and set a new record for [Ron Howard](/wiki/Ron_Howard "Ron Howard")'s highest-grossing opening weekend, overtaking *[Ransom](/wiki/Ransom_(1996_film) "Ransom (1996 film)")* (1996).[[61]](#cite_note-HolidayHearts-63) Upon its opening, the film went on to reach the number one spot at the box office, beating *[Charlie's Angels](/wiki/Charlie%27s_Angels_(2000_film) "Charlie's Angels (2000 film)")*, *[Rugrats in Paris: The Movie](/wiki/Rugrats_in_Paris:_The_Movie "Rugrats in Paris: The Movie")*, *[The 6th Day](/wiki/The_6th_Day "The 6th Day")* and *[Bounce](/wiki/Bounce_(film) "Bounce (film)")*.[[61]](#cite_note-HolidayHearts-63) It held the record for the highest-grossing opening weekend for a Christmas-themed film for 18 years, until the [2018 animated version](/wiki/The_Grinch_(film) "The Grinch (film)") of *The Grinch* surpassed it with $67.6 million.[[62]](#cite_note-64)
